Fixed. Preloop was "running" but not actually working.

## Status now
- `preloop.service` active, API 200 on `/_apis/connectionData`.
- Golden fork base rebuilt and ready (16:19:52), runner `preloop-runner-0-1` up.
- **0** provisioning failures since restart (was 214 in the preceding 6h).
- Guest clock matches host exactly (`16:20:03` == `16:20:03`).

## What was wrong
Since 11:04 UTC no job could get a runner. Every provisioning attempt died at:

```
apt: Release file for .../noble-updates/InRelease is not valid yet
     (invalid for another 2h 14min 26s)   ← identical on every retry
```

Chain of evidence:
1. Host clock was fine (chrony synced, RTC correct).
2. Guest clock in a live provisioning VM read **11:04:14** while host read **16:04:24** — ~5h behind.
3. The resident golden `preloop-runner-golden-3577f5d5a384` booted at **11:04:12** and was then `frozen`. Runners fork from it, so each fork resumed with the golden's frozen wall clock + its own uptime.
4. Constant countdown across retries confirmed it: the skew never shrank, because every fork restarted from the same stale epoch.

apt refuses an index whose `Date` is in the guest's future, so `apt-get update` exited 100, provisioning failed, orchestrator retried every ~28s forever.

Restarting the service forced a fresh golden bake; `apt-get update` in it now exits 0.

## Latent bug worth filing
Nothing resyncs guest wall clock on fork/thaw — the fork base's clock is frozen at bake time and inherited by every runner. The skew equals how long the golden has sat frozen, so this recurs whenever a golden survives a few hours without a fingerprint change (exactly what happened after this morning's reboot: golden baked 11:04, still in use at 16:04). Options, cheapest first: have the agent set time from the host on thaw/exec, run `hwclock -s`/chrony at fork start, or refuse a fork base older than N minutes.

Unrelated pre-existing noise seen in logs: GitHub App 4429171 still isn't subscribed to the webhook events preloop needs (`check_run`, `check_suite`, `workflow_run`, …), so those deliveries never arrive.

arguments.code:
script = r'''
set -e
J=/var/lib/preloop/state/github-app.json
APP_ID=$(sudo jq -r .app_id $J)
sudo jq -r .private_key_pem $J > /tmp/pk.pem
chmod 600 /tmp/pk.pem
b64() { openssl base64 -A | tr '+/' '-_' | tr -d '='; }
NOW=$(date +%s)
HDR=$(printf '{"alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT"}' | b64)
PAY=$(printf '{"iat":%d,"exp":%d,"iss":"%s"}' $((NOW-60)) $((NOW+540)) "$APP_ID" | b64)
SIG=$(printf '%s.%s' "$HDR" "$PAY" | openssl dgst -sha256 -sign /tmp/pk.pem | b64)
JWT="$HDR.$PAY.$SIG"
echo "app_id=$APP_ID"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  https://api.github.com/app > /tmp/app.json
echo "--- slug/name:"; jq -r '.slug, .name, .id' /tmp/app.json
echo "--- events:"; jq -c '.events' /tmp/app.json
echo "--- permissions:"; jq -c '.permissions' /tmp/app.json
echo "--- hook config:"
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $JWT" -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  https://api.github.com/app/hook/config | jq -c .
rm -f /tmp/pk.pem
'''
import base64
b = base64.b64encode(script.encode()).decode()
print(len(b))
open('/tmp/probe_b64.txt','w').write(b)

fn build_rejuvenation_script(clone: &str, seed: &str, record: &VmRecord) -> String {

    let ssh_block = if root.is_empty() {
        "if ls /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
             KG=''; for k in /usr/bin/ssh-keygen /bin/ssh-keygen /usr/local/bin/ssh-keygen; do \
                 if [ -x \"$k\" ]; then KG=\"$k\"; break; fi; \
             done; \
             if [ -z \"$KG\" ]; then echo 'no ssh-keygen to rotate the host keys' >&2; exit 42; fi; \
             rm -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub; \
             \"$KG\" -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; \
             if ! ls /etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
                 echo 'host key rotation produced no keys' >&2; exit 42; \
             fi; \
         fi"
            .to_string()
    } else {
        format!(
            "if ls {root}/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
                 CH=''; for c in /usr/sbin/chroot /sbin/chroot /usr/bin/chroot; do \
                     if [ -x \"$c\" ]; then CH=\"$c\"; break; fi; \
                 done; \
                 KG=''; for k in /usr/bin/ssh-keygen /bin/ssh-keygen /usr/local/bin/ssh-keygen; do \
                     if [ -x {root}\"$k\" ]; then KG=\"$k\"; break; fi; \
                 done; \
                 if [ -z \"$CH\" ] || [ -z \"$KG\" ]; then \
                     echo 'no chroot/ssh-keygen to rotate the workload host keys' >&2; exit 42; \
                 fi; \
                 rm -f {root}/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key {root}/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key.pub; \
                 MADE=''; mkdir -p {root}/dev; \
                 for d in 'urandom c 1 9' 'random c 1 8' 'null c 1 3'; do \
                     set -- $d; \
                     if [ ! -e {root}/dev/$1 ] && mknod -m 666 {root}/dev/$1 $2 $3 $4 2>/dev/null; then \
                         MADE=\"$MADE {root}/dev/$1\"; \
                     fi; \
                 done; \
                 \"$CH\" {root} \"$KG\" -A >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; \
                 if [ -n \"$MADE\" ]; then rm -f $MADE; fi; \
                 if ! ls {root}/etc/ssh/ssh_host_*_key >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
                     echo 'host key rotation produced no keys' >&2; exit 42; \
                 fi; \
             fi"
        )
    };
    format!(
        "set -e; \
         {require_root}\
         hostname '{c}' 2>/dev/null || true; \
         printf '%s\\n' '{c}' > {root}/etc/hostname; \
         tr -d '-' < /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid > {root}/etc/machine-id; \
         if [ -f {root}/var/lib/dbus/machine-id ] && [ ! -L {root}/var/lib/dbus/machine-id ]; then \
             tr -d '-' < /proc/sys/kernel/random/uuid > {root}/var/lib/dbus/machine-id; \
         fi; \
         {ssh_block}; \
         rm -rf {root}/var/lib/cloud/instance {root}/var/lib/cloud/instances/* {root}/var/lib/cloud/data/instance-id 2>/dev/null || true; \
         printf '%s' '{s}' > /dev/urandom 2>/dev/null || true; \
         umask 077; \
         mkdir -p '{state_dir}'; \
         printf '%s\n' smolvm-forkpoint-restored-v1 > '{restored}'; \
         true",
        c = clone,
        s = seed,
        state_dir = smolvm_protocol::forkpoint::STATE_DIR,
        restored = smolvm_protocol::forkpoint::RESTORED_PATH,
    )
}

Both answered. Full write-ups below.

---

# 1. smolvm bug: forked clones inherit the golden's wall clock, forever

**Repo:** `/Users/bnjoroge/smolvm` (deployed build: smolvm 1.8.3)

## Statement

A CoW fork restores the golden's guest memory, which includes the guest's `CLOCK_REALTIME` state. Nothing re-seeds it in the clone. So every clone's wall clock equals **the instant the forkpoint was created, plus the clone's own uptime** — i.e. the clone is behind real time by the *wall-clock age of the forkpoint*, and it never catches up.

## Reproduction (no preloop needed)

```sh
smolvm machine start --name golden --forkable --image ubuntu:24.04
# let it reach its forkpoint, then age the forkpoint deliberately:
sleep 900

smolvm machine fork --golden golden --name clone1
smolvm machine exec --name clone1 -- sh -c 'date -u; cut -d. -f1 /proc/uptime'
date -u    # host
```

**Expected:** clone within ~1s of host.
**Actual:** clone is ~15 min behind, and the identity holds exactly:

```
guest_now == forkpoint_creation_time + clone_uptime
```

Increase `sleep` and the skew grows 1:1. The clone never self-corrects — verified against a clone with **652 s uptime**, still 3 m 27 s behind (well past the 60 s timesync interval).

### Production measurement backing this

| | |
|---|---|
| `golden fork base ready` logged at | `16:19:52` |
| clone `preloop-runner-0-2` guest clock | `16:30:44` |
| clone uptime | `652 s` |
| $16{:}30{:}44 - 652\,\text{s}$ | $= 16{:}19{:}52$ — exactly the forkpoint |
| host at time of reading | `16:34:11` (skew $3\,\text{m}\,27\,\text{s}$) |

Earlier the same day, a golden baked at `11:04:12` was still the fork base at `16:04` → every clone booted **5 h** behind, which broke apt in all of them:

```
E: Release file for .../noble-updates/InRelease is not valid yet
   (invalid for another 2h 14min 26s)
```

The countdown was byte-identical across 214 consecutive attempts — the tell that the base epoch is fixed, not drifting.

## Why the two existing safety nets both miss

**`crates/smolvm-agent/src/main.rs:180-201` — `maybe_set_clock_from_host()`**

```rust
const Y2020_SECS: i64 = 1_577_836_800;
...
if now_secs >= Y2020_SECS { return; }   // ← bails here
```

Designed for WHP guests booting at ~1999. A clone inherits a clock that is stale but plainly post-2020, so the guard returns early. Also irrelevant in the clone regardless: `main()` never re-runs — the restored guest resumes *past* it.

**`crates/smolvm-agent/src/timesync.rs` + `main.rs:246` — `timesync::spawn()`**

Receives host `CLOCK_REALTIME` pushes on vsock DGRAM port 123. Its own header scopes it: *"On hypervisors without a guest-readable paravirt clock (macOS/HVF and Windows/WHP), libkrun's host-side `TimesyncThread` pushes…"*. On the Linux/KVM host there is no such push — empirically proven by the 652 s-uptime clone still being 3 m 27 s off, when the documented interval is 60 s. The fallback that saves macOS sleep (issue #521) simply does not fire here.

## Fix site

`src/agent/fork.rs::build_rejuvenation_script` (~lines 959–1020) already exists precisely to scrub state that goes stale on a fork. It rejuvenates hostname, `machine-id`, dbus id, SSH host keys, cloud-init instance state, and the RNG seed — **but not the clock**, which is the same class of inherited-stale state.

The script is host-generated and already interpolates host-side values (`{s}` = seed), and runs as root in the guest, so the minimal fix is one interpolated statement:

```sh
date -s @{host_epoch_at_fork} >/dev/null 2>&1 || true;
```

Alternatives, in order of increasing scope: have the guest agent re-seed on seeing `RESTORED_PATH`; or run libkrun's `TimesyncThread` on Linux/KVM too, which would also bound drift for long-lived clones.

## Blast radius beyond apt

Any signed/time-bounded material inside a clone: TLS `notBefore` validation, JWT/OIDC `iat`/`exp`, registration-token expiry against the control plane, and every job log/artifact timestamp.

## Note for preloop's side of this

Goldens are keyed by content fingerprint only, with no age bound — `crates/preloop-orchestrator/src/environment.rs:372` says it outright: *"the pool silently keeps the old golden forever"*. So on any server that runs for hours without a fingerprint change, the skew grows until apt breaks. **This will recur on `main`.** Until smolvm is fixed, the durable mitigation is a golden TTL (re-bake when the fork base exceeds ~1 h) rather than a manual `systemctl restart preloop`.

---

# 2. The GitHub App genuinely isn't subscribed — and one warning entry is a preloop bug

I minted an app JWT on `main` with the deployed PEM and asked GitHub directly:

```
app_id=4429171   slug=aksh-dogfood-app
events:      ["pull_request","push"]
permissions: {"checks":"write","contents":"read","metadata":"read","pull_requests":"read"}
hook url:    https://aksh.preloop.dev/api/v1/github/webhooks
```

So preloop's warning is reporting GitHub's own answer accurately (`github_app.rs::read_app_events_at` just reads `GET /app` → `.events`). Two separate things are going on.

## a) Why your ticks didn't take: permission gating

GitHub only renders an event checkbox if the app holds the permission that event belongs to. With the four permissions above:

| Event | Needs | Status |
|---|---|---|
| `issues`, `issue_comment` | **Issues** | permission absent → checkbox never appears |
| `workflow_run` | **Actions** | permission absent → checkbox never appears |
| `check_run`, `check_suite` | Checks ✓ | allowed, but unticked |
| `create`, `delete`, `release`, `repository_dispatch`, `workflow_dispatch` | Contents ✓ | allowed, but unticked |
| `pull_request_review` | Pull requests ✓ | allowed, but unticked |

So the fix is two steps, in order: **add the Issues and Actions permissions first**, save, then the missing checkboxes appear and can be ticked. Permission additions also have to be **accepted for the installation** (GitHub emails an approval / shows it under the install's settings) before those events actually flow.

For the second group — allowed by current permissions yet still unticked — the likely causes are editing a different app or the page not being saved. Worth confirming you were on **`aksh-dogfood-app` (id 4429171)**, since that's the one this server authenticates as. Permission→event mapping above is from GitHub's docs, so double-check it against the UI as you go. `[INFERENCE]`

## b) `pull_request_target` is a preloop bug — that one can never be satisfied

`crates/preloop-runner-server/src/github_app.rs::required_trigger_events()` lists `pull_request_target`. That is **not a webhook event** — it's a workflow `on:` trigger, fed by the ordinary `pull_request` delivery. GitHub's webhook events reference contains **0** occurrences of it (against 18 for `pull_request_review`, 9 for `workflow_run`).

Consequence: even after you tick every real event, `/app` can never return `pull_request_target`, so `warn_missing_trigger_events` fires on every startup forever — alarm fatigue on a warning that's supposed to mean something. It should be dropped from the list (its coverage is implied by `pull_request`).

## Impact right now

Low for core CI: push/PR checks work, which is why runs are executing. The missing events only disable the extra triggers (`workflow_dispatch`, `issue_comment` commands, `check_run` re-runs, `release`, etc.).

---

## Current state of `main`

Service active, API 200, golden re-baked at 16:19:52, runners `-0-1`/`-0-2`/`-0-3` registering and executing job steps, **0** provisioning failures since the restart (against 214 in the previous 6 h). The clock skew is already back to ~3.5 min and climbing at 1:1 with wall time — it becomes fatal again once it exceeds the age of Ubuntu's published index, so the golden TTL is the thing worth doing before tomorrow.

sources.title: Using the REST API to interact with checks - GitHub Docs
sources.snippet:
If you create a check run without creating a check suite, GitHub creates the check suite for you automatically. Write permission for the REST API to interact with checks is only available to GitHub Apps.
When this occurs, the GitHub App that created the check run will receive the check_run webhook requesting a new check run. If you create a check run without creating a check suite, GitHub creates the check suite for you automatically. Write permission for the REST API to interact with checks is only available to GitHub Apps.
OAuth apps and authenticated users can view check runs and check suites, but they are not able to create them. If you aren't building a GitHub App, you might be interested in using the REST API to interact with commit statuses. To use the endpoints to manage check runs, the GitHub App must have the checks:write permission and can also subscribe to the check_run webhook.
To use the endpoints to manage check suites, the GitHub App must have the checks:write permission and can also subscribe to the check_suite webhook.
By default, GitHub creates a check suite automatically when code is pushed to the repository. This default flow sends the check_suite event (with requested action) to all GitHub Apps that have the checks:write permission. When your GitHub App receives the check_suite event, it can create new check runs for the latest commit.

content.text:
Now it's much clearer, and my earlier answer was slightly over-stated. Here's the simpler version. ## The one-line version preloop isn't guessing whether you ticked the boxes — it asks GitHub, and **GitHub says the app is subscribed to only `push` and `pull_request`**. Some of what you ticked was likely never tickable, because GitHub hides event checkboxes for permissions the app doesn't have. ## The evidence, plainly I minted a JWT with the app's own key on `main` and asked two questions. What the app *claims* to be subscribed to (`GET /app`): ``` events: ["pull_request", "push"] permissions: {"checks":"write", "contents":"read", "metadata":"read", "pull_requests":"read"} ``` What GitHub has *actually delivered* (last 100 webhook deliveries): ``` 60 pull_request 18 push 17 check_suite ``` Those agree — with one bonus, explained below. ## The mental model: two separate gates People expect one list. There are two, and the first controls the second. ```mermaid graph LR A[Gate 1: Permissions
what the app may READ] --> B[Gate 2: Event subscriptions
which events GitHub SENDS] B --> C[Webhook delivered to preloop] ``` **Gate 1 — Permissions.** Your app has four: Checks (write), Contents (read), Metadata (read), Pull requests (read). **Gate 2 — "Subscribe to events" checkboxes.** GitHub only *renders a checkbox* for an event whose permission you already hold. Miss the permission and the checkbox isn't unticked — **it isn't on the page at all**. That's why the ticking felt like it worked but didn't stick for some events: you can't tick what isn't shown. | Event you want | Needs permission | Do you have it? | |---|---|---| | `issues`, `issue_comment` | **Issues** | ❌ — checkbox not displayed | | `workflow_run` | **Actions** | ❌ — checkbox not displayed | | `pull_request_review` | Pull requests | ✅ shown, just unticked | | `create`, `delete`, `release`, `repository_dispatch`, `workflow_dispatch` | Contents | ✅ shown, just unticked | So it splits into two different problems: **3 events are blocked by missing permissions**, and **6 events were tickable all along** — for those, the likely explanation is editing a different app, or the page not being saved. Worth confirming you were editing `aksh-dogfood-app`, id **4429171** — that's the identity this server authenticates as. ## Correction to what I told you earlier The warning **over-reports**. Three of the entries it lists as "missing" aren't real problems: - **`check_suite` and `check_run`** — per GitHub's docs, *"GitHub Apps with write-level access for the 'Checks' permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event."* Your app has `checks: write`, so these arrive without ever appearing in the `events` list. The 17 `check_suite` deliveries above are the proof. Nothing to do here. - **`pull_request_target`** — not a webhook event at all. It's a workflow `on:` trigger, driven by the ordinary `pull_request` webhook. GitHub can never report it as subscribed, so this warning line is a preloop bug that will fire forever. So the genuine gap is **9 events**, not 12. ## What to actually do 1. Decide if you even need them. Core CI is unaffected — `push`, `pull_request` and `check_suite` are flowing, which is exactly why your PR checks work. The gap only disables extra triggers: manual `workflow_dispatch`, `/`-style `issue_comment` commands, tag/branch `create`/`delete`, `release`. 2. If you want them: **add the Issues and Actions permissions first**, save, and only then do the `issues` / `issue_comment` / `workflow_run` checkboxes appear. 3. Adding permissions triggers an **installation approval** — GitHub will not deliver under the new permissions until the `preloopdev` installation accepts them. 4. Tick the 6 already-available ones (`pull_request_review`, `workflow_dispatch`, `repository_dispatch`, `create`, `delete`, `release`) and save. 5. On the preloop side, drop `pull_request_target` from `required_trigger_events()` and treat `check_run`/`check_suite` as satisfied when the app holds `checks: write` — otherwise the warning stays permanently noisy and you'll learn to ignore a diagnostic that's supposed to mean something.

sources.snippet:
trigger a webhook event called repository_dispatch when you want activity that happens outside of GitHub to trigger a GitHub Actions workflow or GitHub App webhook. Processes that happen outside of GitHub should not be given any more than the permissions they explicitly need, and certainly not permission to write repository contents.
Just wanted to ping you to hear if there are any plans to update what permissions are required for repository_dispatch (and I guess also workflow_dispatch)? Right now they both require read and write to repository contents, which makes them tricky to use for integrations with external systems. Basically, we're reluctant to give external sources write-access to the repo (I know there are branch protection rules etc, but still). It would have been awesome if there was a more narrow permission that we could use, that would only allow triggering the repository_dispatch event.

Neither, actually — you're mixing up two separate things that share the name. ## The checkbox is in the App's own settings, not in your repo It lives in exactly one place, global to the app — not per-PR, not in the Actions tab: ``` https://github.com/settings/apps/aksh-dogfood-app/permissions ``` That page is titled **"Permissions & events"**. Scroll past the permissions to the **"Subscribe to events"** section at the bottom — it's a flat list of checkboxes (`Check run`, `Create`, `Delete`, `Issues`, `Release`, `Workflow dispatch`, …). Tick `Workflow dispatch`, hit **Save changes**. It applies to the whole app across every repo it's installed on. Your repo's UI never shows it. ## The Actions-tab thing is a different mechanism The **"Run workflow" button** in the Actions tab is per-workflow, and appears when a workflow file declares `on: workflow_dispatch` (and the file exists on the **default branch** — a common gotcha, since it won't show up for a workflow that only exists on a feature branch). So the two connect like this: ```mermaid graph LR A["Run workflow button
(Actions tab)
or POST dispatch API"] -->|emits| B[workflow_dispatch event] B --> C{App subscribed?} C -->|checkbox ticked| D[Delivered to preloop] C -->|not ticked| E[Dropped, never sent] ``` The button **emits**; the App checkbox decides whether preloop **hears about it**. Two different surfaces, both needed for that path to work end-to-end. Good news on this one: `workflow_dispatch` only requires the Contents permission (docs [4], confirmed above), and your app already has `contents: read`. So unlike `issues`/`workflow_run`, that checkbox is already visible on the page right now — it's simply unticked. ## You may not need any of this If your goal is just "manually kick off a run in preloop," the webhook path is a detour. The deployed binary already does it directly: ``` --event Simulate a trigger event (push, pull_request, merge_group, …) ``` So `preloop run --event workflow_dispatch` runs a dispatch-only workflow locally with no GitHub round-trip, no checkbox, no permission change. The webhook subscription only matters if you specifically want *clicking the button on github.com* to drive a preloop run.

content.text:
That's the one — the webhook warning. Here's exactly what's wrong with it.

## The bug

`crates/preloop-runner-server/src/github_app.rs:1338` — `required_trigger_events()` lists 14 events that preloop compares against what `GET /app` reports. Three of those entries can **never** appear in that response, so the warning can never go quiet:

- **`pull_request_target`** — not a webhook event at all. It's a workflow `on:` trigger, fed by the ordinary `pull_request` delivery. GitHub has no such event to report, so this line is permanently unsatisfiable.
- **`check_run` and `check_suite`** — auto-subscribed for any app with `checks: write` (GitHub docs: *"GitHub Apps with write-level access for the 'Checks' permission are automatically subscribed to this webhook event"*). They're delivered but never listed in `.events`. Your app proves it: 17 `check_suite` deliveries while `.events` says only `["pull_request","push"]`.

## Why it matters

The warning fires from three call sites — `bootstrap.rs:499`, `bootstrap.rs:520` (every startup), and `github_app.rs:1317` (after every webhook-config update). So a **perfectly configured app still gets warned at every boot**, forever. That's a diagnostic that cries wolf, and operators learn to scroll past it — which defeats the point of writing it in the first place.

It also actively misled us today: it told you to go tick `check_suite`, which was already working fine.

## Why the test didn't catch it

`github_app.rs:2222`:

```rust
let complete = required_trigger_events()
    .iter()
    .map(|event| (*event).to_owned())
    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
assert!(missing_trigger_events(&complete).is_empty(), …);
```

It builds the "complete subscription" *from the list under test*. Tautology — it verifies internal consistency and passes no matter how many fictional event names the list contains.

## Fix shape

1. Drop `pull_request_target` (its coverage is implied by `pull_request`).
2. Make `check_run`/`check_suite` conditional on the Checks permission. `read_app_events_at` already fetches the `GET /app` body that carries `.permissions` — it just discards everything but `.events`, so this is widening one return type, not a new API call.
3. Report the **required permission** next to each genuinely-missing event (`issues` → Issues, `workflow_run` → Actions). Right now the message says "tick the missing events" for events whose checkbox GitHub doesn't render — which is precisely the dead end you hit.
4. Replace the tautological test with a hardcoded literal of real event names, so a fictional entry fails CI.

That's independent of the other bug from earlier — the smolvm fork clock skew plus the missing golden TTL, which is the one that actually took CI down for five hours.

Want me to patch the warning? It's contained: one list, one permission-aware branch, plus the message and test. `just test-ci` after.

+/// A webhook event preloop turns into runs, paired with the repository
+/// permission GitHub gates its subscription on.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub(crate) struct TriggerEvent {
+    /// Event name exactly as GitHub reports it in `GET /app`'s `events`.
+    pub event: &'static str,
+    /// `GET /app` permission key that must be granted before the event can be
+    /// subscribed to. The App settings UI does not render an event's checkbox
+    /// while its permission is missing, so reporting the event alone sends the
+    /// operator looking for a control that is not on the page.
+    pub permission: &'static str,
+    /// GitHub subscribes Apps holding `permission: write` to this event
+    /// automatically and never lists it in `events`, so its absence from the
+    /// subscription proves nothing (`check_run`, `check_suite`).
+    pub implicit_with_write: bool,
+}
+
+/// Webhook events a preloop GitHub App must receive for the full CI surface to
+/// work (D7). These are the Tier A + trigger events the adapters turn into
+/// runs; without delivery of one, no workflow YAML can trigger on it.
+///
+/// Every entry must be a real webhook event that `GET /app` can report.
+/// `pull_request_target` is deliberately absent: it is a workflow trigger
+/// preloop synthesizes from the `pull_request` webhook (`events/pull_request.rs`),
+/// not an event GitHub delivers, so requiring it here warned forever.
+///
+/// Permissions mirror each event's "To subscribe to this event, a GitHub App
+/// must have at least read-level access for the … permission" clause in
+/// GitHub's webhook events reference.
+pub(crate) fn required_trigger_events() -> &'static [TriggerEvent] {
+    const fn event(event: &'static str, permission: &'static str) -> TriggerEvent {
+        TriggerEvent {
+            event,
+            permission,
+            implicit_with_write: false,
+        }
+    }
+    const fn implicit(event: &'static str, permission: &'static str) -> TriggerEvent {
+        TriggerEvent {
+            event,
+            permission,
+            implicit_with_write: true,
+        }
+    }
+    &[
+        event("push", "contents"),
+        event("pull_request", "pull_requests"),
+        event("pull_request_review", "pull_requests"),
+        event("workflow_dispatch", "contents"),
+        event("workflow_run", "actions"),
+        event("repository_dispatch", "contents"),
+        event("issue_comment", "issues"),
+        event("issues", "issues"),
+        implicit("check_run", "checks"),
+        implicit("check_suite", "checks"),
+        event("create", "contents"),
+        event("delete", "contents"),
+        event("release", "contents"),
+    ]
+}
+
+/// A required event GitHub does not currently deliver to preloop.
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub(crate) struct MissingTriggerEvent {
+    pub event: &'static str,
+    pub permission: &'static str,
+    /// Whether the App already holds the gating permission — i.e. whether the
+    /// operator can tick the checkbox today or must widen permissions first.
+    pub permission_granted: bool,
+}
+
+/// The required trigger events `subscription` does not cover, in canonical order.
+pub(crate) fn missing_trigger_events(subscription: &AppSubscription) -> Vec<MissingTriggerEvent> {
+    required_trigger_events()
+        .iter()
+        .filter(|required| !subscription.delivers(required))
+        .map(|required| MissingTriggerEvent {
+            event: required.event,
+            permission: required.permission,
+            permission_granted: subscription.has_permission(required.permission),
+        })
+        .collect()
+}
+
+/// Loudly warn when an App's subscription does not cover the trigger set.
+///
+/// GitHub cannot change an App's event subscription through the API — only the
+/// App settings UI can — so this is a warning with exact instructions, not an
+/// attempt to fix the App. Events whose permission is missing are reported
+/// separately: their checkbox does not exist until the permission is granted
+/// and the installation accepts the change.
+pub(crate) fn warn_missing_trigger_events(app_id: &str, subscription: &AppSubscription) {
+    let missing = missing_trigger_events(subscription);
+    if missing.is_empty() {
+        return;
+    }
+    let all = missing
+        .iter()
+        .map(|missing| missing.event)
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+        .join(", ");
+    let tickable = missing
+        .iter()
+        .filter(|missing| missing.permission_granted)
+        .map(|missing| missing.event)
+        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
+    let mut blocked: BTreeMap<&str, Vec<&str>> = BTreeMap::new();
+    for missing in missing.iter().filter(|missing| !missing.permission_granted) {
+        blocked.entry(missing.permission).or_default().push(missing.event);
+    }
+    let mut steps = Vec::new();
+    if !tickable.is_empty() {
+        steps.push(format!(
+            "tick these under Subscribe to events: {}",
+            tickable.join(", ")
+        ));
+    }
+    if !blocked.is_empty() {
+        let grants = blocked
+            .iter()
+            .map(|(permission, events)| format!("{permission} (for {})", events.join(", ")))
+            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+            .join("; ");
+        steps.push(format!(
+            "grant these permissions first — GitHub hides an event's checkbox \
+             until its permission is granted, and the installation must accept \
+             the change before delivery starts: {grants}"
+        ));
+    }
+    tracing::warn!(
+        app_id,
+        missing = %all,
+        "GitHub App {app_id} does not receive webhook events preloop needs \
+         (missing: {all}). GitHub will never deliver those events to preloop. \
+         Open https://github.com/settings/apps/{app_id}/permissions and {}.",
+        steps.join(", then ")
+    );
+}

+    pub permissions: BTreeMap<String, String>,

+impl AppSubscription {
+    /// Whether the App holds `permission` at any level.
+    fn has_permission(&self, permission: &str) -> bool {
+        self.permissions.contains_key(permission)
+    }

+    /// Whether the App holds `permission` at write level.
+    fn has_write_permission(&self, permission: &str) -> bool {

+            || (required.implicit_with_write && self.has_write_permission(required.permission))
+    }
+}

### Supported events
…
The App-manifest flow (`GET /api/v1/github/register`) defaults to the minimal
CI event set: `push` and `pull_request`. Override the creation-time event list
with `PRELOOP_GITHUB_APP_DEFAULT_EVENTS` (comma-separated) when the App needs
additional or different events. GitHub cannot change an App's event
subscriptions through its API after creation; add later events manually under
the App's settings → Webhooks → Edit.

At startup preloop reads an existing App's subscription back from GitHub
(`GET /app`, App-JWT auth) and **warns loudly** when the trigger events it
turns into runs are missing (`push`, `pull_request`, `pull_request_target`,
`pull_request_review`, `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_run`,
`repository_dispatch`, `issue_comment`, `issues`, `check_run`, `check_suite`,
`create`, `delete`, `release`). GitHub cannot change an App's event
subscription through the API — tick the missing events under the App's
settings → Webhooks → Edit.

### Data Flow diagram:

```mermaid
graph TD
    GH[GitHub Webhook / API] -->|1. Event payload & Signatures| Wh[Webhook Receiver]
    Wh -->|2. Event Type & SHAs| Auth[App Auth Client]
    Auth -->|JWT / App Private Key| GH
…
    Report -->|Checks API / Commit Status| GH
```

+turns into runs are missing (`push`, `pull_request`, `pull_request_review`,
+`workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch`, `issue_comment`,
+`issues`, `check_run`, `check_suite`, `create`, `delete`, `release`). GitHub

+events under the App's settings → Permissions & events → Subscribe to events.

+Two subtleties the warning accounts for, so it stays silent on a correctly
+configured App:
+
+- **Permissions gate the checkboxes.** GitHub only renders an event's checkbox
+  once the App holds the permission that event requires (`issues` → Issues,
+  `workflow_run` → Actions, `create`/`delete`/`release`/`push`/
+  `workflow_dispatch`/`repository_dispatch` → Contents, `pull_request*` → Pull
+  requests). The warning names the permission to grant first; the installation
+  must also accept the widened permissions before delivery starts.
+- **`check_run`/`check_suite` are implicit.** Apps with `checks: write` are
+  auto-subscribed and GitHub never lists these in `events`, so preloop treats
+  write access as satisfying them.
+
+`pull_request_target` is deliberately not in the list: it is a workflow
+trigger preloop synthesizes from the `pull_request` webhook
+(`src/events/pull_request.rs`), never an event GitHub delivers, so requiring a
+subscription to it warned forever.
*** End Patch

content.text:
### Step 1: Set up Webhook in GitHub
1. Go to your GitHub App settings.
2. Set the payload URL to `http://<your-preloop-url>/api/v1/github/webhooks`.
3. Set the content type to `application/json`.
4. Enter a secure Webhook Secret (e.g. `super-secret`).
5. Select the events preloop should turn into runs. For the full surface,
   tick every event in the table above; the manifest flow
   (`GET /api/v1/github/register`) does this automatically for new Apps.
   At minimum, tick the trigger events: `push`, `pull_request`,
   `pull_request_target`, `pull_request_review`, `workflow_dispatch`,
   `workflow_run`, `repository_dispatch`, `issue_comment`, `issues`,
   `check_run`, `check_suite`, `create`, `delete`, `release`.

### Step 2: Start `preloop-runner-server`
Run the server with the environment variables set:
```sh
export PRELOOP_WEBHOOK_SECRET="super-secret"
export PRELOOP_LOCAL_WORKSPACE="/path/to/runner-watcher"
export PRELOOP_GITHUB_TOKEN="ghp_optional_token_for_checks"

just serve
```

arguments.code:
import subprocess
msg = """fix(github-app): stop warning about undeliverable webhook events

The startup subscription check warned forever on a correctly configured
App, because `required_trigger_events()` listed three events `GET /app`
can never report:

- `pull_request_target` is not a webhook event at all. It is a workflow
  trigger preloop synthesizes from the `pull_request` webhook
  (`events/pull_request.rs`), so GitHub has nothing to report and the
  entry could never be satisfied.
- `check_run`/`check_suite` are auto-subscribed for Apps holding
  `checks: write` and are omitted from `events`, so their absence never
  meant they were undelivered. Verified against a live App: 17
  `check_suite` deliveries while `events` was `["pull_request","push"]`.

The warning also told operators to "tick the missing events" for events
whose checkbox GitHub does not render, because the App lacks the gating
permission -- a dead end. It now reads permissions from the same
`GET /app` response and splits its advice: events tickable today, versus
events needing a permission grant (and installation acceptance) first.

`read_app_events_at` becomes `read_app_subscription_at`, returning events
plus permissions as `AppSubscription`; the per-event permission mapping
mirrors each event's "must have at least read-level access for the ..."
clause in GitHub's webhook events reference.

The old test built its "complete subscription" from the table under
test, so it passed for fictional event names. It now asserts every entry
against a literal list of real GitHub webhook events.

Drive-by, unrelated: fix a `clippy::manual_is_multiple_of` error in
store.rs that already failed `just test-ci` on main under Rust 1.97.
"""
print(subprocess.run(["git","commit","-m",msg],cwd="/Users/bnjoroge/preloop",capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
